inferences: This suggests a practical joint project around interpretable site baselines and guarded incremental updates. The proposal is conditional because Kiss's availability is unknown; openness to joint projects does not establish a time commitment.
BACnet behaviour, actual appliance contention and plant-manager understanding remain transfer gaps. Modbus/DNP3 results and previous processor measurements do not establish performance on ProtoSense.

proposedActions: Propose separate training, tuning and held-out client periods; verify temporal independence and operating-mode coverage. Train/calibrate without attack labels. Compare fixed rules, statistical site baselines and an incremental detector; vary contamination and update safeguards individually. Before evaluation, freeze a label-free tuning objective: lowest alert-episode rate subject to agreed resource and baseline-sensitivity constraints, ties favouring simplicity. Evaluate the selected configuration separately for Modbus and BACnet on held-out traffic and isolated-bench injections, including persistent anomalies and process changes. Measure recall, delay, false-alert burden, comprehension, CPU, RAM and forwarding latency. Proposed go/no-go: at least 80% of injected episodes detected within 60 seconds; 95% upper confidence bound at most one false episode per observed site-day; at least 80% correct plant-manager interpretation tasks. Require protocol-specific 95% lower confidence bounds of at least 80% for timely recall and comprehension, using predefined matching, tasks and denominators. Require hardware-budget compliance and no forwarding-latency regression beyond agreed measurement tolerance under representative load. Missing data, insufficient evidence or unsafe testing means no pass, regardless of selected method.

Propose merging alerts for the same site, asset and anomaly type separated by at most five minutes into one episode. Experts review every episode; unresolved episodes count as false. Divide false episodes by fully monitored site-days, accounting for temporal clustering in confidence bounds. Randomly sample all evaluation windows, alerted or not, with equal recorded inclusion probabilities for expert labelling. Window labels assess contamination, not episode-rate numerators; detection claims use only injected or confirmed cases.

Propose six weeks after permissions and staffing confirmation: two for access, coverage and splits; two for replay and safe bench scenarios; two for held-out testing and hardware measurements. Kiss would lead features, calibration and analysis; company engineers support parsing, integration and operator review within part-time capacity. Establish NDA, research-sharing permission and testbed agreements first; collection consent alone is insufficient. Freeze updates during evaluation, separately test operator-approved resets, and document integration, rollback and maintenance ownership.

Do permissions cover research sharing and replay, and are representative BACnet captures, operating logs, safely reproducible scenarios and plant-manager participants available?

content.markdown:
# Site-specific, explainable anomaly detection for ProtoSense

## Verified facts
- ArmaturaSec reports several terabytes of captures collected from consenting clients over three years, but no confirmed malicious examples. It describes a need for site-specific normal-behaviour modelling. [F1]
- ProtoSense inspects Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP. ArmaturaSec reports that excessive false positives caused clients to disable alerts and identifies plant managers as the audience for plain-language explanations. [F2]
- The company uses embedded Linux and reports having on-device inference hardware. Its hardware-variant plan links a dedicated security processor with on-device anomaly detection and packet-forwarding latency. [F3]
- The company's collaboration-access statement names archives, hardware bench, firmware and an NDA. Kiss's testbed-access statement names a data-sharing agreement. The company describes the capture clients as consenting clients. [F4]
- ArmaturaSec offers one to two part-time engineers. Kiss lists openness to joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions. [F5]
- Kiss's Modbus work estimates register-level timing, payload and command-sequence distributions. Her incremental modelling work reports planned process reconfiguration as a persistent anomaly episode. [F6]
- Her Isolation Forest study reports a calibration risk: a tenfold contamination-estimate mismatch reduced average precision from 0.91 to 0.63. Her embedded experiments used Modbus/TCP and DNP3 captures. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The experiment could establish whether site-specific detection offers manageable, understandable alerts on both protocols without compromising appliance operation, before wider deployment.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and permissions, Kiss could test how calibration and guarded adaptation transfer to BACnet and heterogeneous client operations, using operational captures alongside controlled bench evidence.

## Our inference
- This suggests a practical joint project around interpretable site baselines and guarded incremental updates. The proposal is conditional because Kiss's availability is unknown; openness to joint projects does not establish a time commitment.
- BACnet behaviour, actual appliance contention and plant-manager understanding remain transfer gaps. Modbus/DNP3 results and previous processor measurements do not establish performance on ProtoSense.
- The archives should be treated as presumed normal, not ground truth. Undetected compromise, maintenance and seasonality could distort baselines; adaptation could absorb persistent attacks unless operator-approved updates and rollback are tested.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose separate training, tuning and held-out client periods; verify temporal independence and operating-mode coverage. Train/calibrate without attack labels. Compare fixed rules, statistical site baselines and an incremental detector; vary contamination and update safeguards individually. Before evaluation, freeze a label-free tuning objective: lowest alert-episode rate subject to agreed resource and baseline-sensitivity constraints, ties favouring simplicity. Evaluate the selected configuration separately for Modbus and BACnet on held-out traffic and isolated-bench injections, including persistent anomalies and process changes. Measure recall, delay, false-alert burden, comprehension, CPU, RAM and forwarding latency. Proposed go/no-go: at least 80% of injected episodes detected within 60 seconds; 95% upper confidence bound at most one false episode per observed site-day; at least 80% correct plant-manager interpretation tasks. Require protocol-specific 95% lower confidence bounds of at least 80% for timely recall and comprehension, using predefined matching, tasks and denominators. Require hardware-budget compliance and no forwarding-latency regression beyond agreed measurement tolerance under representative load. Missing data, insufficient evidence or unsafe testing means no pass, regardless of selected method.
- Propose merging alerts for the same site, asset and anomaly type separated by at most five minutes into one episode. Experts review every episode; unresolved episodes count as false. Divide false episodes by fully monitored site-days, accounting for temporal clustering in confidence bounds. Randomly sample all evaluation windows, alerted or not, with equal recorded inclusion probabilities for expert labelling. Window labels assess contamination, not episode-rate numerators; detection claims use only injected or confirmed cases.
- Propose six weeks after permissions and staffing confirmation: two for access, coverage and splits; two for replay and safe bench scenarios; two for held-out testing and hardware measurements. Kiss would lead features, calibration and analysis; company engineers support parsing, integration and operator review within part-time capacity. Establish NDA, research-sharing permission and testbed agreements first; collection consent alone is insufficient. Freeze updates during evaluation, separately test operator-approved resets, and document integration, rollback and maintenance ownership.

## Open questions
- Can Kiss confirm availability for this joint project, and can both sides confirm staffing, funding and the proposed schedule?
- Which appliance and security processor are available, and what CPU, memory, traffic-load and forwarding-latency budgets should govern acceptance?
- Do permissions cover research sharing and replay, and are representative BACnet captures, operating logs, safely reproducible scenarios and plant-manager participants available?
- Before testing, can both sides approve one-to-one injection-to-alert matching by asset/type from injection onset, protocol-specific sample sizes and confidence procedures, and representative interpretation tasks covering affected equipment, deviation and appropriate response, with a correctness rubric and all assigned tasks as denominator, alongside alert adjudication, tuning constraints, update approvals and maintenance ownership?
